More than one hundred years after the Parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, there was a king named Aśoka, also known as King Aśoka, who ruled over Jambudvīpa.
Kings from various nations vied with one another to come and pay their respects to him, inquiring about his methods for eliminating calamities.
Dharma. At that time, the people within King Aśoka’s realm were for the most part afflicted by poverty, hunger, cold, and nakedness.
Unable to remain standing,
the Great King then went to the Kukkutarama Monastery and paid homage to the assembly of monks.
He also described the state of poverty and suffering among the people.
At that time, there was a bhikṣu in the assembly named Tulu-zhi.
Emerging from the midst of the great assembly, he addressed the king, saying,
"The wish-fulfilling jewel shall bring benefit and aid to sentient beings.
The king said:
"How should one obtain the wish-fulfilling jewel?
The bhikṣu replied,
"One should practice ten kinds of dharmas."
First, because of seeking Buddhahood,
one gives away acquired wealth and possessions to sentient beings.
Second, because of seeking the Dharma.
Third, for the sake of making offerings to the Sangha;
fourth, for the sake of bringing peace and stability to the land;
fifth, for the sake of rescuing the people.
Sixth, for the sake of skillfully constructing and enshrining stūpas and temples;
seventh, for the sake of intimidating neighboring kingdoms;
eighth, for the sake of seeking the ritual implements of Śakra.
Ninth, for the sake of making offerings to the Buddha;
tenth, for the sake of bringing great wealth and benefit to all people.
This should be done on the first day of the first month.
Light seven lamps;
in each location, offer one hundred and twenty bowls of lamps to the celestial images.
Furthermore, fashion an image of Śākyamuni Tathāgata and adorn it.
It is hoped that there will be many śrāvakas and bodhisattvas surrounding [the Buddha],
like the retinue of a great king.
You should know that the power and efficacy of the Tathāgata are inconceivable.
Those who make offerings to him will certainly obtain the wish-fulfilling jewel.
Therefore, Great King,
you should make offerings to the Buddha.
Those who make offerings to the Buddha hang silk banners and canopies and burn the most sublime incense.
On the eighth day of the second month,
he entered the sea to gather treasures;
before a month had passed, he obtained precious jewels.
Furthermore, one shall obtain a wish-fulfilling jewel (cintāmaṇi).
There are two kinds of jewels:
the first is the Great Wish-Fulfilling Jewel.
The second is the minor *ṛddhi* (supernatural power).
As for the minor *ṛddhi*,
it is that which one first attains upon making a request.
As for the "Great Wish-fulfilling Jewel," it naturally rains down treasures upon heaven and earth. Great King,
you should know that one who seeks the Great Wish-fulfilling Jewel [should act thus].
Seek it within the mind;
do not look for other methods elsewhere.
Among these seven dharmas:
There is nothing that does not benefit the people of the land.
Why is this? It is because they cease from seeing the practices of plundering and killing.
He amassed great treasuries,
which harmed the people;
they could no longer endure this and naturally rose in rebellion.
When fathers, sons, and brothers are appointed to official posts and granted households by the state,
they instead wish for chaos and turmoil;
as disorder does not cease, the national laws are utterly destroyed.
"Who shall assist the Great King in governing Jambudvīpa?
May the Great King grant amnesty to the prisoners in the jails;
those aged fifty shall be exempted from their labor."
It causes the poor to serve the wealthy so that they may sustain their lives;
this is a great wish-fulfilling jewel for the salvation of sentient beings,
not a precious gem that rains down wealth to relieve them.
After the Great King passed away,
the kingdom was divided and the people perished in flight.
The Tathāgata’s True Dharma revolves throughout the ten directions;
city walls crumble and fall,
and officials become like the mountains and wilds.
The King should reflect three times upon matters that benefit the people.
Furthermore, for those minor kings scattered throughout the world who, in this degenerate age, greedily admire and ardently desire the King’s Dharma,
they should practice the Dharma of lighting lamps.

At that time, there was a bhikṣu from the kingdom of South India who had formerly been a non-Buddhist but had left the household life out of admiration for the Dharma.
As he said to King Śveta:
"In the past, while seeking among external teachings, I found a dharma that benefits the people;
today, I have left the household life to enter into the Buddha-dharma."
There are also dharmas that benefit sentient beings.
First, talismans can summon wealth and treasures,
which are obtained according to the local conditions of the land.
Second, by longing for the healing of the illnesses of sentient beings,
they are cured as soon as the treatment is applied.
Third, the True Dharma can cause wind and rain to follow their proper seasons.

all dragons and spirits follow my commands.
Furthermore, take willow wood and carve it into human form.

then, having encircled the sides of the altar, recite the mantra as follows:
"I take refuge in Śakra, Lord of Devas."
The Wind Deity comes to succor sentient beings;
the Fire Deity comes to give rise to radiance;
the Rain Deity comes so that the hundred grains may ripen to maturity.

when the earth deity arrives, sentient beings are brought to peace and stability.

If one writes talismans and places them where mountain deities reside, [the same effect follows].
May the winds and rains be timely and harmonious.
By inscribing this talisman to avoid calamities upon the head,
and placing it before the heart to attract wealth, may these aims be fulfilled.
If you write this talisman and place it beneath your feet,
you will be able to walk [upon water]. This talisman can exhaust the waters of the sea and can cause mountains and peaks to crumble.
If a transcendent (ṛṣi) obtains it, he can transform heaven and earth;
if an ordinary person obtains it, they are transformed into a great immortal elixir.
[This occurs on] the fifth day of the fifth month.
Take one *bīja* (seed) of ox-gallstone, as large as a sparrow;
four *liang* of ginger;

On the seventh day of the seventh month,

If a person suffers from all manner of illnesses—vomiting, water-retention, abdominal pain, swelling of the four limbs, sudden wind-attacks, headaches, cholera, mental distress, severe constipation, or inability to breathe—[this remedy shall be applied].
Take the aforementioned medicinal pills;
each pill is the size of a small bean.
Administer two pills to the patient.

whether appearing old or young.
Suffering from many ailments, such as chronic fevers, errors in treatment, exhaustion, and cold-natured disorders;

The third talisman ensures that one’s own person will not encounter calamity or misfortune for a hundred years,
and it neutralizes flying corpses (*fei-shi*), various demonic influences, and malevolent curses.
Write [the mantra] in vermilion on a piece of silk seven inches long and wear it;
for a man on the left and for a woman on the right.
One should recite the name of the Great Seer Vasu while burning incense, and all evils will be kept far away.
The fourth talisman masters the rite for causing a husband and wife to loathe one another like water and fire,
so that they curse each other with loud voices and cannot find a livelihood through their disputes.
Use seven inches of silk.
Write this talisman and wear it for great good fortune.
For males, on the left; for females, on the right.

May the filial piety and righteousness between father and son endure for a thousand years.

Eleventh: When traveling, coming and going, or performing any activity, one shall not encounter thieves or be harmed by venomous insects;
when passing through official checkpoints, one need not consult the calendar regarding auspicious days or times.
Write this talisman on silk and wear it; when you travel back and forth, you will encounter those who see you and they shall be joyful, honoring you according to their desires.
Furthermore, tigers and wolves will crouch and hide away.
Thieves shall be avoided and banished;

they should write the talisman in vermilion on raw silk and wear it;

Fortune, rank, and official position will arrive of their own accord;
one's livelihood will be profitable,
and all shall remain as they were originally, without distinction.

Regarding the *Miyue Tujing* (Secret Decision Diagram Scripture) of the Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna: for those who wish to seek the status of a transcendent immortal (*ṛṣi*), longevity, and freedom from aging, [this scripture provides the method].
When one's physical appearance undergoes transformation, one can command spirits and ghosts;
in all such cases, one must maintain purity through fasting and precepts,
cultivating virtue and practicing the Way.
One should serve with a diligent mind,
severing attachment to flavors and purifying the physical basis;
one must not harbor anger or utter insults.
Establish a divine altar at the place of death and rebirth.
First, place the seat of Nāgārjuna within the room;
in each corner, face inward and offer various fruits, milk-rice, and incense.

if there is any fresh fruit or food, [it should be offered].

Once the practice of the Way is completed.

each shall exit through the gate from which they entered; in ten thousand cases,

red is most auspicious. A red mark on the upper left corner of the back of the seal signifies a karmic connection with a relative from a previous life.

The mantra for consecrating fire is *namo bhagavate namo kūṣmāṇḍebhyo namo nimbapāke svāhā*. Whenever one wishes to consecrate fire:
Twice seven times, lick the fire with the tongue to extinguish all sufferings of gold.
Recite twice to protect all medicinal herbs and people.
When one wishes to compound the medicine,
various gods and spirits compete to come and take its flavor; thus,
when people consume it, they often fail to obtain its full efficacy.

and immediately wrote down the divine talismans of the Heavenly Emperor for them.
Furthermore, apply the talismanic scripts of the Six Divine Kings over the painful area.
Consecrate it with pure water using a willow branch and perform the *asura*-prohibiting rite. Once this is completed, [proceed].
Having tied knots with five-colored threads at the painful locations and having sealed them with the Vajra Heart Mudrā,
burn incense and perform prostrations once more to offer prayers.
If on that night one should send a spirit to attend to them, they will be healed and restored to clarity through treatment in a dream.
If, for seven days, one maintains the purification retreat without interruption—
abstaining from alcohol, meat, the five pungent vegetables, rape-seed oil, abusive speech, false speech, sexual misconduct, theft, and killing— [the illness shall be cured].
If one commits [this practice] in this manner,
the illness will not exceed seven days;
it will be cured according to one's wish without doubt— this is a great proven efficacy.
The Celestial Emperor’s Divine Talisman:
written in vermilion to seal off ignorance; write it with careful scrutiny.
It cures the myriad illnesses of humans when swallowed.

If one wishes to break this talisman, the six stars of the Southern Dipper preside over the six musical scales; they enter the human body from above and govern the six talismans. One need not inquire further, for all is known therein. If one practices with light incense and pure clarity, the efficacy will increase.
The Talisman of the Six Supreme Divine Kings.
A talisman for curing ten thousand illnesses.
Write it while burning incense and maintaining purity.
If one writes it upon the place where a person is afflicted,
the illness will immediately disperse and leave the body;
write it with clear precision.
It possesses great spiritual efficacy.
Regarding the method for taking incense: the *Fuxiang fangfa lun* (Treatise on the Method for Taking Incense) states:

"In all practices of reciting mantras as well as in the arts of sound and the measurement of time by water-clocks, when the ears are clear and penetrating, one should take aromatic medicinal substances as the mantra."

The mantra is as follows: *Buddha-nubhadra, umā-jotari, lena lena dhamani, āpa āpa maṃsiri, svāhā*. Take one *jin* each of the following: white *candana* (sandalwood) incense, *agaru* (aloewood) incense, *kunkuma* (saffron) incense, *śrīkhaṇḍa* (white sandalwood) incense, *turuṣka* (bdellium) incense, *jātī-phala* (nutmeg) incense, *tvak* (cinnamon) incense, *elā* (cardamom) incense, *spṛkkā* (sweet flag) incense, *kuṅkuma* (saffron) incense, *mustaka* (costus) incense, and *śatapuṣpā* (hundred-flower) incense. These should be gathered according to the season and dried in the shade. Also take one *jin* of *harītakī*.
The treatise says:
In a single clean room,
within a clean mortar.
Grind each ingredient separately and mix them with honey.
Keep them in a vessel out of the wind and sunlight.
Prior to this, one must abstain from alcohol, meat, the five pungent roots, various flavors, and mustard greens.
Observe the fasts and purify oneself by bathing with fragrant water;
wear fresh and clean garments;
and rinse the mouth with water until the spoon returns [empty].
Sit upright and recite the mantra.
Offer incense seven times.
Then, take one *fūncun* (a square inch) of the medicine with well-water three times daily for seven days.
Chant the mantra seven times and take [the medicine] once.
For twenty-one days, do not leave the precincts of the *maṇḍala* and take it while observing the precepts.
When one hundred days are complete, one’s nature will become spontaneously free.
The multitude of deities uphold it.
When they behold the conduct of the various Buddhas with their own eyes, its fragrance is immediately fresh and pervasive;
after walking ten paces for the second seven-day period, they perceive its fragrance.
After four weeks, he could smell fragrances at a distance of a hundred paces;
after seven weeks, his eyes could see and his ears hear sounds, and he perceived fragrant scents;
all people respected and loved him.
Deities and spirits will provide assistance.
If one burns incense in a secluded place according to one's natural needs,
the various gods will arrive of their own accord.
After wearing it for a full thousand days,
even inanimate objects will become fragrant;
one can even pre-emptively perceive the scent of the flesh of the twelve zodiac signs, as well as that of fish and turtles.
He knew in advance that those vapors were authentic, and he was able to resolve all other vapors belonging to the world.
He used earth to form a mound and, blowing three times through his mouth, incinerated the soil.
The fragrance of that land is exceedingly sharp and beneficial;
wherever there are defiled places or spots where things have died,
one should sprinkle water upon them.
The ground there is entirely fragrant.
If the bodies of those who have died have not yet passed seven days,
when water is poured over them, their corpses will even disintegrate.
It constantly emits a fragrant aroma that brings benefit.
Whenever one has food, take water from a well and infuse it with the incense one is wearing.
Mix it with honey and form pills the size of a弹丸 (a pellet).
Purify the mouth by reciting this mantra one hundred times and cast it into well water;
all that water will become fragrant, and those who drink it will be made to smell sweet.
If there is an evil person possessed by a malevolent spirit,
one should take this incense, which is the size of a pellet, and recite the mantra over it a hundred times; then, having bound it,
place it before the throat of the patient.
The malevolent spirits will disperse.
If there are empty pavilions or wilderness dwellings where many evil ghosts frequently harm people,
one should mix this incense with honey into a ball the size of a pellet.
Burn it with fire;
all the evils within that chamber will be completely extinguished.
The Commentary says:
For all who consume incense,
its root source is a mantra;
it is the very foundation of spirits and deities.
The practitioner should carefully avoid seeing corpses,
as well as the birth-milk, blood, and fluids of domestic animals after giving birth,
and women or small children.
As well as the sounds of chickens and dogs;
one should always purify the body and rinse the mouth,
and whenever seeing filth or impurity, [one should avoid it].
One must necessarily purify defilements through incantation.
Recite the mantra over water three times and use it to wash one's face and eyes.
Only then may one enter the chamber.
Otherwise, the rite will not be accomplished,
and one will incur misfortune and harm.
If sores break out on the body,
one must not recite mantras while visiting various rooms or dwelling quarters.
Furthermore, upon entering a pure chamber,
do not transmit this to those who are unworthy.
Take care that it does not circulate in the world, lest it cause harm to others.
Ṭaṭa ṭara | Ṭaṭa lulu re | Mahā-lulu re | A-ra-ma-ra | Tā-ra-svā-hā. If a person sleeps...
Recite this mantra over water one thousand times;
use it to wash the eyes and face while reciting it.
